reachable: Yes, and the mechanism gets real gradient throughout training. The loss is training-only; it never runs at scoring time, so the read-position question is about whether it shapes the weights that are later read at the withheld-observation position, and it does. Verified by an 80-step real training run with the candidate's own genome (arch r22_prefix_content_xattention, optim r18 bs=64, stream r3, head r2, target identity) on the encoded cups root: the listwise contrastive term is 68% of the loss in the first 10 steps and still 48% at step 80, with mean nll 0.68 and median 0.37 — nowhere near saturation, so the negative-mixture reweighting is live, not a vanished term. (An earlier synthetic probe that added iid noise to tgt appeared to show the contrastive term collapsing to 2-3% of the gradient; that is an artifact — iid noise shifts the distance to every candidate equally and so leaves the ranking untouched. Do not read that result as a finding.) Gradient reaches pred through dist2 only; all weighting (precision, ring, group, collide, neg_w, focal, row_w, q, gate) is computed under torch.no_grad or on detached tensors, as intended. Cost: 0.077 s/step for the loss at n=1905 rows on CPU, versus 0.038 s for parent r12 and 0.056 s for parent r22 — roughly a 2x loss-side cost, consistent with the author's \"one extra n-by-n matmul, unmeasured\".
solves_outside_model: No. This is a pure loss function. It never touches b[\"tok\"], never writes to any tensor the model is fed, never runs at scoring time, and contains no string handling at all — no command parsing, no path parsing, no move resolution, nothing resembling the retracted stream that stamped a resolved answer into a command token. Its only side-information is ctx[\"cmd\"] (the command token the model itself was fed, read detached, used only to form a cosine Gram matrix) and ctx[\"prev\"] (the strict-causal shift of the target matrix the harness builds). Both are read-only; I checked for in-place mutation and there is none. The gating signal that could have been the classic trap — a mechanism keyed on an observation being present, which silently switches off at the withheld scored position — is confined to training: _segment_ids keys on an all-zero previous observation, which is a property of the harness's prev_full construction and is never evaluated during measurement. Choosing which comparisons the gradient pays attention to is exactly the permitted side of the line.
summary:
The installed impl is byte-identical to the proposal file; there is no INTEGRATION_FIX.md. Two of the three headline mechanisms are implemented exactly as described, and I verified them by execution on real encoded data rather than by reading.

WHAT CHECKS OUT.
(1) The exact-target equivalence quotient is correct. On a real 1905-row batch the off-diagonal target distances have a clean gap — 11.084% of pairs below 1e-7 and 11.111% below 1e-5, then nothing until 0.1 — so _EQ_EPS=1e-5 merges numerically-equal targets and nothing else; zero non-transitive triples, so class_size is a genuine equivalence class size. Mean class size 212, max 632 of 1905, consistent with the ~31% constant-observation rate the author measured.
(2) The segmentation claim is exactly right. _segment_ids reproduces the true per-sequence partition with zero merge errors and zero split errors on a real collated batch (exactly 64 all-zero prev rows for 64 sequences). The stronger claim — errors can only split, never merge — holds structurally, since prev_full[:,0] is constructed as zeros.
(3) The board-local component is precisely as advertised and is the strongest part of the proposal: 100.00% of the group budget lands on same-trajectory candidates, effective support 16 (matching the ~17 distinct observations per trajectory), and total negative mass on same-trajectory candidates rises from 1.51% (plain uniform quotient — the author's stated ~1.5% baseline, reproduced to three digits) to 36.1%.
(4) The mass bookkeeping is exact: neg_w row sums are 1.000000 for every row, pos_w row sums 1.000000, nll never negative, and with ctx=None both the group and collision shares fold back into uniform with row sums still exactly 1.
(5) Anti-collapse holds in the claimed direction on real data: perfect prediction 0.0027, constant-row prediction 3.14, batch-mean constant 1.27. The author's toy figures (0.0002 / 0.023 / 2.15 / 2.19) are not reproducible without their toy, and the ordering of the two constant cases inverts here, but the substantive claim — a constant prediction does not minimize it — is true.

WHAT DOES NOT. The command-collision component is roughly an order of magnitude weaker than the hypothesis asserts. sigmoid((z-2.0)/0.5) has no floor truncation, so across ~1900 candidates the sub-threshold bulk absorbs most of the 25% budget. Same-command-different-target candidates end up with 2.2-2.5% of the negative mass, not 25%; the uplift over uniform is 2.4-2.6x, not ~25x; and the row upweighting is close to a uniform 1.8x rescale rather than a selective doubling. The component is not inert — its top-1 pick is a same-command candidate 42-44% of the time against a 0.9% base rate — but it is a soft command-similarity miner, which is nearer the author's own stated failure mode than to their claim.

NET. The code is valid, the structure it will be archived and recombined under (four-component mixture with fixed renormalized budgets, quotiented occurrence mass, board-local negatives) is exactly what the code does, and nothing is solved outside the model. The one thing that is misdescribed is how much of the negative mass the name-collision half actually captures — which is half the candidate's name and the whole of its stated comp_ca story ("Component 2 manufactures that signal directly and it has real mass in this data").

divergences.claim: Component 2 (COMMAND-COLLISION, budget 0.25) "selects the candidates whose COMMAND is a near-duplicate of the anchor's command while the ANSWER is different" and "here they own a quarter of the negative mass" (versus being "ordinary negatives at weight ~1 among ~1500 in-batch candidates" under the parents).
divergences.what_the_code_does: The component receives 25% of the row's negative mass, but its internal distribution is diffuse, not an upper-tail selection. sigmoid((z-2.0)/0.5) is never truncated: at z=0 it is 0.018, and summed over ~1900 candidates the sub-threshold bulk carries roughly as much mass as the tail. Measured on real batches (bs=64, n~1900 rows, the genome's own r3 stream, 4 independent draws): only 6.5-7.4% of the 25% budget lands on same-command-different-target candidates. Total negative mass on those pairs is 2.2-2.5% (5.2% on the 845/1905 rows that actually have such a candidate), versus 0.90-1.05% under the plain occurrence-quotiented uniform — an uplift of 2.4-2.6x, not the ~25x the sentence asserts. Effective support of the collision distribution is 234-297 candidates (median) against 1003-1042 for uniform; only 20% of the collision budget sits in the top 1% of the row. The component does have real directional signal at the very top (top-1 collide candidate is a same-command candidate 42-44% of the time, against a 0.9% base rate), so it is not inert — it is a soft command-similarity reweighting, roughly 10x weaker than the prose claims. The author pre-disclosed a related failure mode in the WHAT WOULD HAVE TO BE TRUE FOR IT TO FAIL section, but predicted the wrong cause (r3 hash code swamping the cosine); the actual cause is the missing floor truncation.
divergences.evidence: Reproduced with the installed impl on data/dockerfs3-cupsF-treat-nocwd train split, r3_srcdst_hashslot_coding.collate, harness-identical prev/cmd construction. 4 batches: coll-budget-frac-on-same-cmd 0.0685/0.0654/0.0741/0.0733; total neg mass on same-cmd-diff-tgt 0.0232/0.0224/0.0252/0.0246 vs uniform 0.0091/0.0090/0.0105/0.0094. Same-src-path variant: 11.1% of budget vs 1.5% uniform (7.5x). top-k precision of collide: top-1 0.444 same-cmd / 0.553 same-src, decaying to 0.230 / 0.361 at top-50.

divergences.claim: Colliding rows are "additionally double the row's weight" (row_w = inv_class * (1 + 1.0 * max_j collide)).
divergences.what_the_code_does: Because collide has no floor, max_j collide is near 1 for almost every row. Measured multiplier quantiles (1 + amax): p10 1.50, p50 1.84, p90 1.97, max 1.97. Rows that genuinely have a same-command-different-target candidate in the batch get mean 1.966; all other rows get mean 1.646. After the row_norm normalization the relative differential is 1.19x, not a selective doubling. The archived DESCRIPTION's "Rows whose command collides with a different target are additionally upweighted in the listwise average" is true only weakly; in practice this is close to a uniform rescale.
divergences.evidence: collide.amax quantiles [0.186, 0.497, 0.837, 0.966, 0.966] on the n=1905 real batch; mean multiplier 1.9656 on the 845 ambiguous rows vs 1.6461 on the other 1060.

divergences.claim: "43 distinct command strings produce more than one distinct output, and 299 of 724 steps (41%) are steps whose command does NOT determine its observation."
divergences.what_the_code_does: The unrestricted numbers on evolve/jail_data/train_sample.jsonl are 54 command strings and 332 steps (46%). The author's 43/299/41% reproduce EXACTLY once steps whose observation is the constant empty-output string are excluded — a restriction the sentence does not state. The measurement is defensible; the sentence as written is not literally what is in the sample.
divergences.evidence: Recomputed with realenv.seq_worldmodel.render_obs over all 24 trajectories / 724 steps: all=54 cmds/332 steps (46%); excluding observations ending in 'exit=0\n' with empty output=43 cmds/299 steps (41%). Every other sample statistic in the hypothesis reproduces exactly: 724 steps, 227 (31%) carry 'cwd=/ exit=0\n', 63% of steps have a duplicated observation, 'cat /tmp/w/cvar/g0/s0.dat' appears with 21 distinct contents, 48 intra-trajectory re-read steps across 13 of 24 trajectories, ~17 distinct observations per trajectory.
